articles.title: Trump’s Iran Deal: A Fragile Pause in a Devastating War
articles.summary: A U.S.-Iran memorandum promises to halt a 3.5-month conflict that’s killed thousands and rocked the global economy. But Israel’s ongoing strikes in Lebanon and defiance from Netanyahu’s government threaten the 60-day truce before it starts.

articles.title: 30 Years After Landmark ILO Convention, Home-Based Workers Still Fight for Equality
articles.summary: Convention 177 recognized home-based workers as equal to traditional wage earners in 1996. Yet only 13 nations have ratified it, and in India, women like Shehnaz Bano earn just 100 rupees per leather jacket piece with no social protections.

articles.title: Sibling Rivalry Goes Global: Brothers Could Clash at the World Cup
articles.summary: Desire and Guela Doue, brothers from Angers, France, could face each other on June 30 if France and Ivory Coast meet in the World Cup’s round of 32. They’re among four sets of siblings playing for different nations this summer.
